title: Sprite2Ds not rendering in specific scenes.
body:
### Tested versions

v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8]

### System information

Godot v4.3.stable - Windows 10.0.19045 - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (Intel Corporation; 32.0.101.5972) - 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1160G7 @ 1.20GHz (8 Threads)

### Issue description

A simple scene with a root node of type Node2D and a single Sprite2D node, with no scripts and everything as the default setting, can sometimes not render the Sprite2D. I experienced multiple scenes in my project no longer render any Sprite2D nodes, and discovered that the problem remains when removing all other potential factors. In an MRP, this is the only scene in the project with everything as default. 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d5212af-5eb2-4fe4-be3d-cd95c3438dc3)
The texture on the Sprite2D is assigned to the default icon.svg, and it does appear as if it should be rendered based on the texture preview in the inspector. 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b65d69b-ef80-40a1-a612-4e33473c60e2)
Yet in the editor, the Sprite2D is not rendered, and displays as such:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/620c58a2-b321-448d-b8fd-1da289025470)
Running the scene will also not render the Sprite2D. 

In my experiments, I discovered that changing "top level" to true in the inspector for the Sprite2D makes it render as expected, for some reason. Adding a Node as shown between the Sprite2D and the Node2D will also have this effect.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e47208c-6d5d-42c1-ad7c-cb1db45d2187)

The only workaround I've found when this occurs is to just make a new, identical scene. 


### Steps to reproduce

Unfortunately, I don't know how to make this issue occur in a scene, it happened multiple times while I was editing some larger scenes with a variety of nodes and scripts. One thing that may or may not be relevant is that I was changing the type of a few nodes which were parents to multiple Sprite2Ds from Node2Ds to a custom node type I use which extends Node2D. I know very little about how the engine operates under the hood, but my best guess is that this is some sort of corruption of the scene, as making a new identical scene does not have the same issues. At any rate, I've attached my MRP below, perhaps it can be used to find the source of the problem. 

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)
[MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17594603/MRP.zip)
